claims: Every nonempty finite candidate set over a linear order has a unique minimum.
The canonical selector returns a member of the candidate set and is less than or equal to every candidate.
Enlarging a candidate set can only improve or preserve the selected minimum.
Filtering a candidate set can only worsen or preserve the selected minimum when the filtered set remains nonempty.
For any batch tie over a total key, the canonical winner is deterministic and unique.
Selecting a singleton containing the selected winner is idempotent.
proof_method: Lean Finset minimum and maximum primitives
